ePošťák — Peppol e-invoicing

Sends and receives Peppol e-invoices and business responses through the Slovak access point ePošťák, with your own ePošťák contract or through the Data Dance hosted service.

Version19.0.1.1.1
EditionCommunity and Enterprise
LicenceAGPL-3
Requiresedi_base_peppol, edi_epostak_base

What it is for

ePošťák is a Slovak Peppol access point. These modules connect Odoo to it, so that the e-invoices prepared by Peppol e-invoicing actually leave and arrive:

Module Role
this module makes ePošťák the transport for Peppol documents
edi_epostak_base the sandbox / production switch, the firm ID, the Peppol address checks
edi_epostak_connector_sapi the connection itself: credentials, sending, collecting, delivery status, reachability check
edi_epostak_broker_client (delivered separately) only on the Data Dance hosted service: sends through the hosting broker instead of holding ePošťák credentials (below)

Install this module and the connector. What is sent, when, and what happens to received documents is decided by the Peppol module — its guide explains routing, sending, receiving and business responses. This guide covers what is specific to ePošťák: the connection, what each status means and what to do when something fails.

The Slovak e-invoicing obligation from 1 January 2027 is summarised in the legal background of the Peppol guide.

Setting it up

Everything is in Settings → EDI, section ePošťák. The environment applies to the whole database; the Firm ID, the credentials (on the hosted service, the broker key) and the inbound poll belong to the company you are working in. To set up another company, switch to it and fill in its own.

  1. Environment (ePošťák Environment): Sandbox (default) or Production. While the sandbox is active a yellow banner says so; sandbox documents never reach the real Peppol network. Each environment keeps its own credentials, so switching does not erase them.
  2. Credentials for the active environment — block Credentials (Sandbox) or Credentials (Production): Client ID and Client Secret from your ePošťák account. The URL fields are prefilled and normally stay as they are. On the hosted service, fill in the broker instead (below).
  3. Configured key tells you which kind of secret you entered — it cannot be read back from the password field:
Key Firm ID
firm key (sk_live_…) leave ePošťák Firm ID empty; the firm is implied
integrator key (sk_int_…), speaking for several firms ePošťák Firm ID is required: the UUID of the firm this database invoices as
  1. Test Connection. Saves the settings and tries to log in. With an integrator key and no Firm ID it lists the firms the key may act for, with their IČO and Peppol address; if there is exactly one, it fills in the company's Firm ID for you. It also names any other company that allows e-invoicing but has no ePošťák credentials of its own. Press it again to confirm. The result is always shown as a notification — a failure does not discard what you typed.
  2. Your company's Peppol address — on your company's contact, tab Invoicing: Peppol e-address (EAS) 0245 and your DIČ as the endpoint (see the Slovak identifier). Every request to ePošťák is made as that participant. An endpoint under scheme 0245 that is not exactly ten digits is refused before anything is sent; eight digits is reported as an IČO, which is not routable.
  3. The company switches in the same Settings page, block Peppol BIS3 (this company) — allow e-invoicing, scope, automatic sending, purchase journal: see the Peppol setup. With more than one Peppol provider installed, set Peppol Transport there; left empty, nothing goes through Peppol.
  4. Check a customer before the first invoice — see reachability.

Only system administrators open Settings; to send and see EDI messages they also need the EDI groups (access).

Through the Data Dance hosted service

On a database hosted by Data Dance, edi_epostak_broker_client (delivered separately) is installed and the connection goes through the hosting service's broker rather than straight to ePošťák. The database then holds no ePošťák credentials at all. In Settings → EDI → ePošťák, block Data Dance broker:

Field What it is
Broker URL Setting it switches the database to broker mode; clearing it returns to a direct ePošťák contract
Broker key ID identifies the key; not secret on its own — per company
Broker key signs every request; shown once when it is issued — per company

You receive these with the hosted service. The Client ID, Client Secret and Firm ID are then neither used nor needed — the broker decides which companies the database may act for. Test Connection asks the broker exactly that and reports an error if it lists no company for this database.

Everything else — documents, statuses, collection, the reachability check — works the same. Failures arrive already classified: the database's key was refused, the document or address was refused (fix it, it will fail the same way again), or the service is temporarily unavailable.

What the statuses mean

The EDI message of an ePošťák document moves like this:

State Meaning
Ready the file is generated, waiting to be sent
Queued waiting for EDI: send queued messages (no job runner), which runs every 2 minutes; a message whose send failed temporarily waits here too, with a warning in Error Details
Sent ePošťák accepted the document for transport (HTTP 202). This is intake, not delivery. Provider Interchange ID holds ePošťák's document ID.
Done ePošťák reports the document delivered to the recipient's access point
Error sending failed, or ePošťák reports the document rejected, send failed, delivery failed or validation failed; Error Details holds "ePošťák status: …" with ePošťák's reason

Sent becomes Done or Error through the scheduled action ePošťák: Query Outbound Delivery Status, every 30 minutes, for up to 500 sent messages per run. It needs Track Delivery Status on (default) and a key allowed to read documents (scope documents:read). If ePošťák refuses the status query, tracking is skipped for that run and the messages simply stay Sent — so a message that stays Sent for a long time means "accepted, no delivery confirmation yet", not "delivered".

Delivery to the recipient's access point is not the customer's acceptance. Whether the customer accepts, disputes or pays the invoice arrives, if the customer's system sends it, as an Invoice Response.

When sending fails

What you see Cause What to do
Error, text about credentials, Peppol address, Firm ID or a missing element a configuration or addressing problem found before sending fix the setting or the contact named in the message, then Send
Error, an ePošťák code (e.g. validation) ePošťák refused the document; it will fail the same way again correct the invoice or the contact
Queued, blocking level Warning, with a reason in Error Details a temporary problem: timeout, rate limit, ePošťák or its login unavailable nothing — the next run of the send action tries again

A temporary failure is retried automatically on every run of EDI: send queued messages (no job runner), every 2 minutes, until ePošťák accepts the document or refuses it for good; there is no limit on the number of attempts, and a Retry-After wait requested by ePošťák is not observed beyond that interval. A permanent failure moves the message to Error, where it stays until someone sends it again. One failed document does not stop or undo the others sent in the same run. ePošťák's correlation ID, if it gave one, is in brackets at the end of the error — quote it to ePošťák support.

To retry, press Send on the EDI message (or Actions → Send (queue dispatch) for several). It sends the same file again, and ePošťák recognises it by its idempotency key (Transmission UUID, derived from the file's content): if the earlier attempt had in fact got through before the error, the repeat is collapsed instead of delivered twice. Send via Peppol on the invoice generates the file anew; if anything in it changed, it is a new document to ePošťák.

Receiving

The scheduled action ePošťák: Poll Inbound Documents runs every 30 minutes. For every company with ePošťák credentials of its own it asks, as that company, for the documents waiting for that company's Peppol address (companies sharing one integrator key are still asked one Peppol address at a time), 20 per page and up to 5 pages per run (Documents per Poll Page, Max Pages per Poll), and runs again at once if more are waiting. Each document is stored and processed as described in receiving e-invoices, and only then acknowledged to ePošťák, which removes it from the queue there. A document whose content cannot be fetched is not acknowledged and is tried again next time. The acknowledgement is between Odoo and ePošťák only; the sender receives nothing from it.

Receiving fails silently unless you look, so the connector reports on itself:

  • Last inbound poll in Settings shows, for the company you are working in, "OK at … — N document(s) fetched", "FAILED at … — reason (last success: …)" or "Never polled".
  • Poll inbound now runs that company's collection immediately and says what happened.
  • After Warn after N failed polls consecutive failures (default 3; 0 turns it off) a To-Do "Incoming ePošťák documents are not arriving" is put on your company's contact for the first EDI Manager (else an EDI User, else the administrator). It is closed automatically once collection works again.

Checking a customer's Peppol address

On a contact with a Peppol address, Check Peppol reachability (next to the endpoint, for EDI users) asks the Peppol directory through ePošťák whether that address can receive Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 invoices and credit notes:

Answer Meaning
Reachable on Peppol registered, and accepts BIS 3.0 invoices and credit notes
Registered, but not for BIS3 billing exists on the network, but sending invoices to it will be refused
Not registered on Peppol the directory does not know it — the customer is not on Peppol yet, or the scheme or number is wrong (a Slovak DIČ is scheme 0245, an IČ DPH 9950)

ePošťák's own reason is added when it gives one, and a note if the participant is reported as not network-ready.

Transfer tuning

Block Transfer Tuning; the defaults suit most databases.

Setting Default Purpose
OAuth Scope documents:send documents:read documents:write rights requested at login; documents:send alone can send but not collect or track delivery
Track Delivery Status on query delivery status of sent documents
Warn after N failed polls 3 when to raise the To-Do about failed collection
Documents per Poll Page 20 1 to 100
Max Pages per Poll 5 pages per run before the collection re-schedules itself
Request Timeout (s) 60 per call to ePošťák

Limitations

  • One environment per database. Sandbox or production applies to every company; the credentials and the Firm ID are each company's own. A company that allows e-invoicing without credentials of its own neither sends (its documents end in Error, naming the company) nor collects.
  • A message keeps the environment it was created in while it is being sent; pressing Send via Peppol again generates it anew in the environment active now (see sending).
  • A send that fails permanently is not retried automatically. A temporary failure is retried after ePošťák's Retry-After or a growing pause, at most five times (see sending).
  • Configured key reads "No secret configured yet" in broker mode, which is expected there.
  • Whether ePošťák is a certified provider of the delivery service under § 76a of the VAT Act is a question for ePošťák; this module does not check it.
